newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. asks Mexico to extradite alleged drug lord.
newsitem.headline: U.S. asks Mexico to extradite alleged drug lord.

text.p: The U.S. government has formally asked Mexico to extradite alleged Gulf drug cartel leader Oscar Malherbe de Leon following his capture last month, a Mexico daily reported on Thursday.

In a front-page story, La Jornada quoted a "high-ranking U.S. official" as saying the United States had asked for Malherbe's extradition despite denials by Mexican officials in recent days that such a request had been made.

"We have a completed request for (the extradition) of Malherbe," the newspaper quoted the official as saying. "It is not accurate" to say the United States has not asked for the alleged drug lord's extradition, it quoted him as saying.
Officials at Mexico's Foreign Ministry and the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City were unavailable for comment.

The United States has made it clear that it wants Mexico to extradite Malherbe and considers the case a test of Mexico's willingness to cooperate in the drug war. The issue also comes at a time when the Clinton administration is lobbying Congress to support its recent decision to "certify" Mexico as a reliable anti-drug ally.
Mexico has traditionally refused to extradite its citizens to other countries to stand trial for crimes, preferring instead to try them here.

Malherbe was arrested on Feb. 26 in Mexico City. He is alleged to have been a top lieutenant in the Gulf cartel, who replaced Juan Garcia Abrego as its leader when the drug lord was captured in the city of Monterrey in January 1996.

La Jornada also said the United States has asked Mexico for the provisional arrest of 60 other presumed drug traffickers, both Mexican and U.S. citizens in Mexico, as a first step in their eventual extradition.

"These requests are for a provisional arrest to begin the process (of extradition). Not all these individuals are Mexican, but we have reason to believe they are in Mexico," the newspaper quoted U.S. Justice Department spokesman John Russell as saying.
